content: Unlike today  she thought, pulling her coat tighter ,   Corliss did her best to keep out chill of  the cold autumn air .   “The oath is the bond between the monarchy and the people, it is the trust that is placed into the hands of men and women ,  to stand up against the evil in this world ,  to ensure the victims get the justice they deserve” she repeated  hearing those same words in her mind, told to her from a much younger  Uri   .   “ Crandon , when we take the oath, we do agree to not get married, or have children. We agree to make justice our partner in life ,  and that is not for everyone, but I will tell you there is no higher calling young man, but that does not mean you give up sex , ” she finished ,  shooting a smile at the apprentice as his face   turned red .   “ Y es ,  Warden , ” he whispered but  refused  to meet her eyes.  They continued to ride for a while,  They  came to an open field and nodding to herself Corliss turned to the young man. “ Crandon , have you practiced much with your  SenPai , aside from the initial training?” She asked and watched as the young man’s face lit up.  Every apprentice relished the moment they were able to learn to use the  SenPai . She suppressed a smile as the young apprentice answered, excitement edging his voice “Not really, Warden,” he said, reaching up and exposing the long leather bracer that was strapped to his left arm.  Corliss looked over to see the worn leather tied firmly to his  forearm ,  and  smiled as the sunlight danced over the multicolored runes that had been carved from crystal and inlaid into the leather, the young man ran his fingers over them, the runes beginning to glow slightly as he summoned the power within them.  “Slow down there  Crandon , let’s go over what you know before we start using it . ” she said ,   T he young man pushing the sleeve back down to cover the magical bracer.   “So, what do you know about the  SenPai  Apprentice?” Corliss asked.  Crandon  did his best to hide the eye roll, but she still caught it and suppressed another smile.  “The  SenPai  was commissioned by the first Emperor for the warden’s, it was crafted by the first members of the Order of the Dragon after signing the Agreement” he recited as dry as if it were directly quoted from the textbook.  Time to throw him off a bit .  “Okay, how is it  warden s can use  m agic? Are we  m ages?” she asked and could see another half-suppressed eye roll.  “No. Wardens are not  m ages ,  nor do we wield  m agic, that is the realm of the Mage and the Order .   H owever ,  like everyone ,  we all descend from those with power ,  so we  have the ability to  draw on  that  power ,  to a minor degree .   B ut we do not have the ability to  actually use  it directly .   T hat is where the Senpai comes in , ” he stated ,  almost bored.   “Okay, then how does the  SenPai  work?” she asked watching as the question caught him off guard .  Corliss could see his mind working .   I t was not an easy question —w ardens did not know the finer points of  m agic or  r unic script .   S o, she waited patiently as  Crandon  struggled to form an answer.  He started and then stopped for a moment ,  forming his thoughts and she could hear the struggle in his words as he finally started to answer the question .   “The  SenPai  is a set of runic spells that the Warden can activate giving them abilities such as increased hearing and sight as well as activation of the Spirit Bond” he  answered   and Corliss watched the  triumphant  smile form on his face ,   he had answered well she thought .  “What is the spirit bond,  Crandon ?” Corliss  asked  .   Crandon’s smile faltered a little as his eyes moved back and forth, she could see his mind forming words from pieces of lessons over the past year, then with a nod he spoke .  “We are able to identify with a creature, something that mirror’s our own values and strengths, that animal is amplified and made real through the spell of the  SenPai , giving the Warden a friend in combat and a scout in tracking , ” he  offered,  and his smile grew wider, again he had done  well,  and Corliss conceded the young man had learned well.
